themes_detail.label: Graffiti Explosion in Flatbush
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints surged to 97 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 2.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 4,211% spike (z-score: 39.73)—suggesting either a coordinated tagging campaign, gang activity, or sudden removal of anti-graffiti enforcement in CD 309.
evidence: 97 graffiti complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 2.2 weekly average over 8 weeks prior
Z-score of 39.73 indicates extreme statistical anomaly; severity rated high
44x normal weekly volume suggests acute event rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Canvass blocks with highest complaint density to document scope and identify patterns (tags, artists, locations)
Contact NYPD, NYC Parks, and Department of Sanitation to determine if staffing/enforcement changes coincide with spike

themes_detail.label: Park Rules Violations Spike
themes_detail.summary: Park rules violations jumped to 5 complaints THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1,900% increase (z-score: 10.97)—indicating possible unauthorized activities, overcrowding, or safety issues in Flatbush/PLG parks.
evidence: 5 park rules violation complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 10.97 indicates severe statistical anomaly
Aligns with community board's long-standing request to 'improve access to parks and amenities'
reporting_angles: Visit major parks (Prospect Park, Parade Grounds, Linden Hills) to observe what violations residents are reporting
Interview Parks Enforcement officers and community gardeners to understand what changed this week

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints nearly doubled to 21 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 10.6 per week—a 98% increase (z-score: 4.65)—suggesting new construction, nightlife, or commercial operations expanding in the district.
evidence: 21 commercial noise complaints last week vs. 10.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.65 indicates statistically significant spike
348 building permits filed in past 90 days (202 alterations) may correlate with noise-generating work
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 complaint addresses with DOB permit data to identify which construction/commercial sites are generating complaints
Interview residents near top complaint addresses and nearby businesses to determine source (construction, bars/restaurants, HVAC upgrades)

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Matter Surge
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police complaints quadrupled to 14 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 3.5 per week—a 300% increase (z-score: 4.04)—potentially indicating street-level disorder, quality-of-life crimes, or public safety concerns residents felt compelled to report.
evidence: 14 non-emergency police matter complaints last week vs. 3.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.04 indicates significant statistical anomaly
Surge overlaps with graffiti spike and park violations, suggesting broader quality-of-life deterioration
reporting_angles: FOIL NYPD to obtain non-emergency complaint summaries from last week (311 data may not specify what crimes/issues triggered calls)
Interview precinct captain and community leaders to understand recent street activity and whether police resources have shifted

themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Reports Surge
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints tripled to 6 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 1.5 per week—a 300% increase (z-score: 4.5)—raising sanitation and potential public health concerns, possibly linked to rodent or wildlife management issues.
evidence: 6 dead animal complaints last week vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.5 indicates significant statistical spike
May indicate broader rodent/pest infestation if animals are concentrated in specific locations
reporting_angles: Map the 6 complaint locations to see if they cluster (suggesting localized issue like illegal dumping or food waste mismanagement)
Contact Department of Sanitation and local pest control to learn if they've fielded complaints about rodent/wildlife surge
